positions.as_written: Expect a lateral injury to involve more than this ligament.
Document peroneal nerve function at the first assessment of any lateral injury, because a later deficit cannot then be attributed to treatment.
Treat varus restraint as primarily this ligament and rotational restraint as primarily the other two.
Assess all three primary lateral structures before planning.
Plan the femoral points for this ligament and the popliteus tendon together, because 18 mm of bone has to hold two tunnels that must not converge.
Consider reconstruction rather than repair for a chronic lateral injury, since the vascularity that supports medial healing is not matched here.
Identify the peroneal nerve before any fibular work.
